findings.title: Await the save operations before resolving `saveAll`
findings.explanation: `Array.prototype.forEach` ignores the promises returned by its async callback. Consequently, `saveAll` resolves immediately after scheduling the callbacks, unlike the previous `Promise.all`, and a rejected `item.save()` is not propagated through the returned promise.
findings.user_impact: Callers awaiting `saveAll` can continue before persistence finishes, and save failures can surface as unhandled rejections instead of being handled by the caller.

evidence_items.output_snippet: Any item has an asynchronous `save()` operation; the failure case additionally requires one of those promises to reject.

assumptions: `item.save()` returns a promise or another awaitable value.
Callers rely on the async function's completion and rejection contract.
limitations: No callers or matching tests for `saveAll` were supplied, so downstream manifestations cannot be identified more specifically.

verification_assessment.explanation: forEach invokes each async callback but ignores its returned promise. Because saveAll contains no await tied to those callback promises, its own promise resolves with undefined after iteration completes, potentially before asynchronous item.save() operations settle. A rejection from item.save() rejects only the discarded callback promise and is not propagated through saveAll. The supplied diff also establishes that this replaced an awaited Promise.all.

findings.proposed_remedy: Restore `await Promise.all(items.map(item => item.save()))`. Add a regression test proving the returned promise remains pending until all saves finish and rejects when any save rejects.

findings.title: Bind search values instead of interpolating them into SQL
findings.explanation: Both `user` and `query` are inserted directly into the SQL statement. A value such as `user="' OR 1=1 -- "` changes the predicate and can return expenses belonging to other users. Quotes in legitimate values can also produce a SQLite syntax error. The route's empty-query guard does not protect nonempty input or `user`.
findings.user_impact: An attacker who controls either argument may read expenses outside the requested user's scope or cause search requests to fail.

sql = f"SELECT id, user, amount, description FROM expenses WHERE user = '{user}' AND description LIKE '%{query}%'"

unresolved_assumptions: The supplied scope does not establish how the route obtains or authenticates user, so direct external attacker control of that argument is not proven; query nevertheless reaches the same SQL construction without escaping or binding.
verification_assessment.explanation: The route forwards nonempty user and query values through the service to the repository unchanged. The repository inserts both into SQL syntax with an f-string and executes the resulting text without parameter binding. For example, a user value of `' OR 1=1 -- ` produces a predicate beginning `user = '' OR 1=1 -- `, commenting out the remaining condition and permitting rows for other users. Embedded quotes can likewise alter or invalidate the statement. The route only rejects an empty query and provides no SQL-safety validation.

findings.proposed_remedy: Restore parameter binding: `cursor.execute("... WHERE user = ? AND description LIKE ?", (user, "%" + query + "%"))`. Add a regression test using quotes and an injection payload, verifying results remain restricted to the exact user.

findings.title: forEach discards promises returned by async callbacks
findings.explanation: forEach discards promises returned by async callbacks. Await Promise.all with map, or use an awaited for…of loop when completion order matters.
findings.user_impact: The async function can finish before the operations complete, so failures and completion are not propagated.

evidence_items.output_snippet: forEach discards promises returned by async callbacks. Await Promise.all with map, or use an awaited for…of loop when completion order matters.

verification_assessment.explanation: The callback is async and therefore returns a promise, but Array.prototype.forEach does not consume or await callback return values. saveAll consequently resolves independently of the save promises, and failures from item.save() are not propagated through saveAll.

findings.proposed_remedy: Use await Promise.all(items.map(async ...)) or an awaited for…of loop, depending on ordering requirements.

edits.old_content:
sql = f"SELECT id, user, amount, description FROM expenses WHERE user = '{user}' AND description LIKE '%{query}%'"
        cursor.execute(sql)
edits.replacement:
sql = "SELECT id, user, amount, description FROM expenses WHERE user = ? AND description LIKE ?"
        cursor.execute(sql, (user, "%" + query + "%"))
edits.rationale: Uses SQLite parameter binding for both untrusted values, preventing either value from changing the SQL structure. Building the LIKE pattern as a bound value preserves substring-search behavior, exact user isolation, and support for legitimate quotes.
